Hi Samir — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so your engineering team has a clear view of what we discussed: 

Summary of requirements you outlined:
- Latency targets: P95 < 300ms, P99 < 800ms for streamed chat responses. First-token streaming latency ideally < 200ms for interactive UI.
- Throughput: steady-state ~200 req/s, average response size ~512 tokens, occasional bursts up to ~1000 req/s for 3-7 minutes (marketing-driven spikes).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent conversations ~50-100; spikes may push concurrent sessions briefly into the 400-600 range during campaigns.
- Streaming: required (server-side chunked responses to support progressive render).
- SLO/behavior expectations: no more than 1% request errors during steady-state; during bursts graceful degradation acceptable (queueing / 429s) but want predictable behavior and monitoring.

Autoscaling & burst capacity we discussed:
- You called out needing ~full-service capacity within a couple minutes for sustained bursts, plus a warm-capacity option to reduce cold-starts.
- We recommended a warm pool for the steady burst profile and a separate burst capacity tier for very short spikes.

Immediate next steps:
1) Can you share a 24-hour traffic histogram and a 7-day peak timeline (CSV or Prometheus export) so we can size the warm pool precisely?
2) Confirm whether you need first-token latency SLAs or P95/P99 only.
3) I'll loop in our infra leads (Vivek and Dev) for precise scale-up time and queueing semantics. Expect a technical note + config recommendations by EOD tomorrow.

Attachment: redwood-autoscale-playbook.pdf (summary of warm-pool patterns + config templates)

If that looks right I can capture this as the mutual action plan and send a proposed configuration + pricing for burst add-on.

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi — copying the requested tech details below. Vivek feel free to supplement if you want more infra-specific numbers.

Short answers (customer-ready):
- Scale-up times: 
  - Cold start from zero (provisioning new GPU VM + model load) typically 60-120s depending on instance type and model size.
  - Warm-instance ready -> serving (model already loaded) is ~5-15s (socket & runtime warm-up).
  - Horizontal scale (adding additional warm instances from existing warm pool) is typically 10-30s to register and drain traffic onto them.

- Warm pool behavior & recommendation (based on their burst profile: 1k req/s for ~5 minutes, avg 512 tokens):
  - For 512-token avg responses, our per-request GPU time (token generation + network) averages ~180ms under optimized kernels. (This will vary by model; we should confirm model family.)
  - Start with warm_pool_size = 20 for their region. That gives immediate headroom for short bursts and avoids cold-load for ~400-600 concurrent requests depending on batching.
  - Configure an additional burst_capacity buffer (reserved on-demand nodes) sized for the 1k peak — e.g., reserve 10-15 larger instances that can be spun from cold in ~60-90s but get up to speed quickly when combined with the warm pool.

- Queueing & backpressure:
  - Default request queue per route: 30s. If a request hits the queue longer than that, we return 429 with a structured JSON error explaining "capacity shortfall".
  - Streaming behavior during scale-up: we do not buffer partial streaming chunks server-side indefinitely. If the instance serving a stream is preempted/cold-starts mid-stream, we attempt connection handoff to a warm instance; we buffer up to 5s of outgoing bytes to avoid client-visible gaps. For client resilience we recommend implementing an idempotent resume token on the client so the UI can re-request from the last committed token on a 429 or transient connection error.

- Config examples & recommended knobs to include in the mutual action plan:
  - warm_pool_size: 20
  - warm_pool_min_ready_time: 300s (how long to keep an instance in warm pool before scaling down)
  - prewarm_timeout: 90s (time to attempt cold provisioning before falling back)
  - request_queue_len_seconds: 30
  - burst_capacity_nodes: 10
  - fallback_policy: return_429_after_queue | canary-routing-to-smaller-models

Notes / caveats:
- Model family matters: larger weights increase cold-start by ~30-50s. If FinLynx intends to use a large-parameter chat model, factor that into warm pool sizing or consider model quantization/compiled variants for fast starts.
- We can offer a "burst SLA" add-on (guaranteed warm_pool + reserved burst nodes) that reduces cold start to ~30-60s and commits to <1% request error during advertised burst windows. Pricing is an add-on.

I'll attach a sample autoscale_config_example.yaml (basic template) for their infra team to review.
